title: Gullu’s savings playground
local: Local practice: resets when you leave this tab. No bank or backend connection.
instructions: Choose a goal, then tap a coin to move it from your wallet into the jar. Try a spending choice and compare what remains.
ready: Start with ₹1,000 in fictional coins. Nothing here uses real money.
savedFeedback: Coins saved! Your wallet and goal progress have updated.
spentFeedback: A treat uses ₹50 from the wallet. That is ₹50 less available to save. Undo to try another choice.
insufficient: Your wallet cannot cover that choice. Undo a previous choice or reset to try again.
undone: Choice undone. Your coins are back in the wallet.
resetFeedback: Fresh start: ₹1,000 in the wallet and an empty jar.
milestone: Savings milestone: you have saved at least ₹{amount}!
goalReached: Goal reached! Gullu celebrates your saving choices. Choose a bigger goal or reset and try another plan.
tradeoff: The jar is shared by your goals. Switching goals keeps your coins; it does not create extra savings. Spending now leaves fewer coins for later.
meaning: What you give up when you choose one use for limited money.
example: Spending ₹50 on a treat leaves ₹50 less to put towards a football.
why: Compare what matters to you, then try again. There is room to change your mind.
scenarioInstructions: Choose how to split 100 fictional tokens between two pretend businesses, then explore an event. Your savings jar is unaffected.
oneDown: Business A falls by 20%; B stays unchanged
oneUp: Business A rises by 20%; B stays unchanged
scenarioResult: After this event: {value} fictional tokens (started with 100).
scenarioLesson: Sharing tokens limits the effect of one business falling. It cannot prevent loss when both fall. Explore every event; no choice wins in all situations.
assumptions: Authored hypothetical example, one event, no time or return forecast. Changes of ±20% are teaching assumptions, not market data or guaranteed outcomes. No real-money recommendation.
diversificationMeaning: Spreading exposure across different assets rather than depending on just one.
diversificationExample: Two pretend businesses can react differently to the same event.
diversificationWhy: A mix may reduce concentration risk, but all assets can still lose value.
